verdicts.trueWording: The perpetrator pays a fine of 2d10 GP or works
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the 'Crime' > 'Petty Crime' paragraph of the Roll20 licensed 2024 DMG page (HTTP 200, raw curl with browser UA, HTML stripped). Both limbs hold: the dice expression 2d10 and the coin abbreviation GP sit inside a prose sentence, and the same three-category Crime block also carries 50 GP, 250 GP, 100 GP, 1d6 years and 2d10 years in running prose.

verdicts.trueWording: the River Quarter, Clerkburg, the Artisans' Quarter, and the Foreign Quarter
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that this applies a ward-naming rule the 2014 DMG had set out - the page never mentions the 2014 DMG, any earlier edition, or a ward-naming rule; that link is the claimant's inference, not on this page
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in 'City Neighborhoods'. The naming limb holds on the page's own roster - Artisans' Quarter (a trade), River Quarter (the Selintan River, a physical feature), Foreign Quarter and Thieves'/Slum Quarters (resident classes). Only the cross-edition attribution is unsupported here.

verdicts.trueWording: Clerkburg is the university district of Greyhawk, with dozens of schools
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that each entry runs two or three present-tense sentences - of the eight neighbourhood entries four (Foreign Quarter, Garden Quarter, Slum Quarter, Thieves' Quarter) are a single sentence and none reaches three; the range is one to two
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in 'City Neighborhoods'. The bolding limb is confirmed in the raw HTML, where each entry opens Clerkburg. etc. before the description, and every entry is present tense. Only the sentence-count limb fails.

verdicts.trueWording: the year 576 in the Common Year
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in 'The Big Picture'. The dating limb holds: realm-level events are dated 356 CY (Nyrond joining the secession), 453 CY (accession of King Tavish IV) and 569 CY (Battle of Emridy Meadows). Caveat on form only - the present year is written out as the Common Year in the same parenthesis rather than abbreviated CY, though the abbreviation is used for the dated events.

verdicts.trueWording: Seven years ago, knights and soldiers from Furyondy
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim under 'Central Flanaess' > 'Battle of Emridy Meadows'; the numeral form is in 'The Big Picture' on the same page, which asks the reader to picture the Flanaess about 200 years ago. The no-single-rule limb is reinforced by a second mismatched pair on the page: the Eastern Flanaess culture paragraph writes almost 800 years ago as a numeral while the Western Flanaess paragraph spells out about a thousand years ago, so no consistent spell-out threshold is in force.

verdicts.trueWording: the only relevant details of this history are those that
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the opening sentence of 'Living History', which completes with the clause that they feature in your adventures. The page states it of Greyhawk's own history of ancient empires and recent wars - the claim's generalisation to a setting's history is a fair reading of the worked setting, and the following sentence tells the DM to reveal significant details in the course of adventures.

verdicts.trueWording: provide concrete touchstones to past events
verdicts.note: Verbatim in 'Living History' > 'Echoes of the Past', where all three of the claim's examples appear in one sentence: a crater in the side of a mountain, a defaced statue in the town square, a holiday celebrating a local hero. The page's own word is concrete touchstones rather than physical residue, and the third example (a holiday) is a custom rather than a physical object - a gloss, not a failed limb.

verdicts.trueWording: Summarize what lengthy works say, and focus on the most
verdicts.note: Verbatim as the closing sentence of 'Living History' > 'Historical Records', completing with plot-worthy parts. The page says to focus on the most plot-worthy parts rather than to give only those, so the claim's only is a slight strengthening of the instruction's emphasis.

verdicts.trueWording: Move from the second-person point of view to the third person
verdicts.note: Verbatim as the Tip 1 heading of the article, bylined Shawn Merwin and dated Nov 6, 2019 on dndbeyond.com (HTTP 200, raw curl with browser UA). It is the first of six numbered tips, and the article's opening paragraph equates boxed text with read-aloud text, so both limbs of the claim hold.

verdicts.trueWording: The bloated corpse of a headless dragon dominates the center
verdicts.note: Verbatim inside the Tip 1 body, given as the third-person rewrite (it completes with of a clearing) set against the second-person version he rejects, in which you notice the same corpse. In the preferred form the corpse - the object described - is the grammatical subject and the verb is dominates, exactly as the claim states.

verdicts.trueWording: leave in only the details about the environment when the PCs
verdicts.note: Verbatim under Tip 2 (Avoid the novelist/dramatist urge), introduced as his rule of thumb when writing or editing and completing with the requirement that the PCs must interact with them on some level. The following sentences illustrate with a bog or a monster's stench that matters only as a terrain feature or monster ability.

verdicts.trueWording: boxed text is not the place to unleash that inner novelist
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the first paragraph under the Tip 2 heading, which is itself Avoid the novelist/dramatist urge. The surrounding sentences warn that nothing slows a game more than paragraph after paragraph of boxed text and prose so purple it embarrasses a rainbow, so the claim's novelist's voice reading is exact.

verdicts.trueWording: Describe everything the characters can sense, but not what they can't
verdicts.note: Verbatim as the Tip 3 heading. The body supports the could-not-know limb directly: it faults boxed text that details things the characters couldn't know, giving locked crates whose contents are described as full of mining equipment, and tells the DM to let the mystery linger.

verdicts.trueWording: nothing triggers meta-gaming like the words “seems” or “appears”
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the Tip 4 body (the heading reads Avoid seems to be or appears to be), and the metagaming ground is the page's own reason - those words generally mean some trick or diversion is in the offing. The page frames it as avoidance rather than a formal ban, and directs the DM to let Perception or Investigation checks separate the seems from the is after the boxed text ends.

verdicts.trueWording: If you're the DM, you get two sentences. Period.
verdicts.note: Verbatim under 'Undercover Insight #1: Boxed Text = MEGO' on the Wayback raw capture (HTTP 200), which carries the Design & Development masthead, the date 09/16/2005 and the byline Jesse Decker and David Noonan. The first-person observer is Noonan: the piece describes ditching the Wizards polo shirt to watch games for twenty minutes at a stretch across the four days of Gen Con 2005, and later calls it the Dave wanders around technique. The next sentence supplies the consequence - beyond two sentences players are stacking dice, talking or staring off into space.
